title: Direct Linear-Hull Analysis of PRINTcipher Biases
summary: Weak PRINTcipher keys admit strongly biased linear approximations for any number of rounds, but a direct explanation through the corresponding linear hulls remains open.

formal_statement.body: For PRINTcipher keys that are weak in the sense of the invariant-subspace attack, strongly biased linear approximations exist for any number of rounds, as follows from a link between statistical saturation attacks and multidimensional linear attacks. Directly analyze the corresponding linear hulls to explain these strongly biased linear approximations.

scope.domain: Linear and structural cryptanalysis of PRINTcipher, focusing on biased linear approximations and their linear hulls.
assumptions: The PRINTcipher key is weak in the sense of the invariant-subspace attack.
parameters: Number of rounds, for which the known existence result holds without restriction
scope.unresolved_remainder: Directly explain the strongly biased linear approximations by analyzing the corresponding linear hulls.

citations.label: A Cryptanalysis of PRINTcipher: The Invariant Subspace Attack

progress.summary: The source presents the any-round existence of strongly biased approximations for weak keys as following from a link between statistical saturation and multidimensional linear attacks. It explicitly leaves their direct linear-hull explanation open.
citation_labels: Gregor Leander et al., A Cryptanalysis of PRINTcipher: The Invariant Subspace Attack
